name: CERN'S FOUR DIVISIONS SURVIVE CASTING OUT NINES, checked in one-digit arithmetic that never forms the seven-digit product: for each of the four CMS datasets the published event count and its own files·quotient + remainder agree modulo 9. The lonely theorem cms_events_close_over_their_files decides four exact divisions — events = files·q + r with r below the file count — by multiplying seven-digit numerals. The sealed theorem digital_root defines the ℤ/9 reduction this ledger uses everywhere, carrying 432 % 9 = 0 and the root of every n through 60. THE CROSSING applies that reduction to CERN's divisions and computes the check the original never takes: reduce each factor first, so the kernel decides 8·3 + 0 ≡ 6, 4·8 + 3 ≡ 8, 0·4 + 6 ≡ 6, 4·7 + 3 ≡ 4 (mod 9) — four one-digit multiplications standing in for four seven-digit ones. That is the classical casting-out-nines test, and it is an INDEPENDENT witness to the quotation: a transcription slip in any single digit of an event count moves its residue and the conjunct fails. PERTURBED AND REFUSED: 2079006 to 2079007 — the residue moves and decide refuses. SCOPE: casting out nines is a one-way test. It catches a moved digit; it cannot certify the division, which is what the lonely theorem already does over the full integers. This adds the cheap independent check, not a second proof.

THE FOUR CERN RECORDS CLOSE THEIR TOTALS IN ℤ/9 AS WELL AS IN ℕ: the residues of the four event counts sum to the residue of the published total, and the same holds for the four file counts. The lonely theorem the_four_cern_records_close_their_own_totals adds four seven-digit event counts to 9039615 and four file counts to 502, showing the quotation is internally consistent. The sealed theorem digital_root is the ℤ/9 reduction this ledger computes with. THE CROSSING carries the closure through that reduction, which the lonely theorem never does: the event residues are 6, 8, 6, 4 and they sum to 6 ≡ 6, the total's own residue; the file residues are 8, 4, 0, 4 summing to 7 ≡ 7. So the four records close on BOTH sides of the reduction, and the consistency of CERN's published totals can be rechecked by a reader adding four single digits. PERTURBED AND REFUSED: the event total 9039615 to 9039614, which moves its residue while the parts stay put — decide refuses. SCOPE: agreement mod 9 is necessary, never sufficient; the ℕ closure is the lonely theorem's and stays its own.

THE ENERGY LABEL DOES NOT PREDICT THE WAIT: the two 7TeV records waited 8 and 6 years, the two 8TeV records 7 and 7 — the two classes carry the SAME total embargo, 14 years each. The lonely theorem the_open_data_embargo_ran_six_years_or_longer decides three differences — 2019 − 2011 = 8, 2019 − 2012 = 7, 2017 − 2011 = 6 — and that each is at least six. It says nothing about how the wait distributes. THE CROSSING pairs the differences by the year the data was taken, which is what the energy label names: the 2011 records (7TeV) waited 8 and 6, the 2012 records (8TeV) waited 7 apiece, and 8 + 6 = 7 + 7. The two classes are therefore indistinguishable by total embargo, which is a fact about CERN's release policy that neither the lonely theorem nor the energy theorem states: a longer wait for one 7TeV record is exactly paid for by a shorter wait for the other. PERTURBED AND REFUSED: 6 to 5, which breaks the equality — decide refuses. NAMED AS A COINCIDENCE, NOT AS CONTENT: that shared total is 14, and the ledger separately seals ve_fourteen_faces as 8 + 6 = 14, the same decomposition the 7TeV pair happens to take. Nothing connects a vector equilibrium's faces to a data-release calendar, and this theorem claims no such thing; the content is the EQUALITY of the two totals, which is arithmetic over CERN's own published years. SCOPE: four records, not a policy — a universal drawn from this sample is the fault lean/Cern.lean already refuses by naming "these two" rather than "the run".

THE TWO BEAM ENERGIES ARE 7 AND 8 UNITS OF THEIR OWN DIFFERENCE: 3500 and 4000 GeV per beam have greatest common divisor 500, which is exactly the step between them, so the labels are the unit counts and the two are consecutive, hence coprime. The lonely theorem the_collision_energy_label_step_is_one_tev decides the per-beam halves 7000/2 = 3500, 8000/2 = 4000 and their difference 500. It never asks what the two energies share. THE CROSSING computes that: gcd(3500, 4000) = 500, the step ITSELF, so 3500 = 7·500 and 4000 = 8·500 and the two beam energies are consecutive multiples of their own gap — which is why gcd(7, 8) = 1. The sealed theorem rosette_and_vortex_are_coprime is this ledger's own coprimality fact, carrying gcd 7 9 = 1 beside gcd 7 14 = 7, and it is cited here for the same reason: consecutive integers are coprime, so the run labels "7TeV" and "8TeV" are not merely names but the unit counts of a common quantum, and no finer common step exists. PERTURBED AND REFUSED: 4000 to 4500, where the gap becomes 1000 while the gcd stays 500, so step and gcd part company and decide refuses. SCOPE: an arithmetic relation between two published numerals. Why the machine ran at those energies is CERN's to say.

THE 502 FILES ADMIT NO EVEN SPLIT BUT HALVING: 502 = 2 · 251, and 251 is prime on a bounded search, so the collection's only equal groupings by file are 1, 2, 251 and 502. The lonely theorem the_four_cern_records_close_their_own_totals sums the four file counts to 502 and stops there. THE CROSSING factors that total: 502 = 2 · 251, and no d in [2, 16) divides 251 while 16·16 > 251, which is a complete primality witness by the square bound — so 251 is prime and 502 has exactly four divisors. The consequence is about the collection rather than the numeral: these four records cannot be redistributed into three, four or any other equal number of file-groups; the only balanced split is in half. The four file counts 116, 184, 72, 130 are each even and their greatest common divisor is 2, which is where the single factor of two comes from and why no larger common grouping exists. PERTURBED AND REFUSED: 502 to 500, which is 2 · 250 and NOT twice a prime — decide refuses the factorisation. SCOPE: an arithmetic property of the published file counts of these four records, and of nothing else; another harvest sums to another number.
